{
  "B_expression": "-1/8",
  "C_expression": "-1/2 + u/2",
  "derivation": "Restore the parent P07_W1 program (D1). The active program for this stage was D0 (B=-1/8, C=-1/2 constant). The numerical feedback confirms the dominant residual term with D0 is -u^2*r: for LEFT:x=1/4:s=0, u=-0.1339, r=-5.99e-6, the predicted -u^2*r=+1.08e-7 matches the observed residual 1.07e-7; for UNIFORM:x=1/8:s=0, u=0.007878, r=-1.08e-6, predicted +6.7e-11 matches observed 6.73e-11. Setting C=-1/2+u/2 adds u^2*r/2 to g via the u*r*C channel, so 2*u*g gains +u^2*r, which cancels the -u^2*r from the pure-remainder channel. The residual then reduces to -r^3/8 - 3ur^2/4 + O(r^4, ur^3, u^2r^2, u^3r), all degree >= 3 with no isolated cubic cross-term. For the observed (r,u) pairs the new leading terms are O(1e-12) or smaller. Both bodies are polynomials (constant and linear), hence C-infinity on all of R^2, smooth on any open neighborhood of the closed outer rectangle. The chi_r/chi_u gating is unchanged; outside the inner support the correction vanishes and g=r/2 applies.",
  "inspect": [{"file_id": "CALC/draft.json", "limit": 4096, "offset": 0}],
  "note": "D1 restored from D0. The u/2 term in C cancels the -u^2*r cubic cross-term that was the dominant residual with constant C. Successor stages with accumulated u (|u| up to ~1/8 inside chi_u support) will see residuals drop from O(u^2*r) to O(u^2*r^2, u^3*r, r^3, ur^2). If a later stage shows u approaching 1/8 with visible ur^2 or u^2*r^2 terms, a u^2 component in C or an r-linear term in B could be explored, but at current tau=1/64-1/512 scale the D1 remainder is below 1e-11 for all in-support rows. ZERO rows remain z=1.0 unchanged. Rows with |u|>1/4 (e.g., LEFT:x=1/8:s=0 with u=-0.625, large-z rows) are outside chi_u support and receive no correction regardless of B,C. No analytic-domain certificate beyond polynomial smoothness is claimed."
}
